RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the December 18, 2008/Agrahayana 27, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region; Environment
and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and  U rban Poverty Alleviation;
Information and Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions;
Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways; Space;
Statistics and Programme Implementation; Urban
 Development; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
82
Dump of wastage in coastal areas of
Tamil Nadu
*241. SHRI A. ELA V ARASAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
some foreign companies have dumped the
wastage of their products into the coastal
areas of Tamil Nadu;
(b) if so, the steps taken by
Government;
(c) whether Government has given any
instruction to the State Governments which
allowed foreign companies to dump their
wastage causing severe negative
consequences to the land and future
generations; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Indians apprehended in Belgium
†*242. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that, recently,
Belgium Government has caught 200
Indians who were to be illegally taken to
England;
(b) whether it is also a fact that human
traffickers had kept these Indians in a
pitiable condition;
(c) whether it is also a fact that such a
racket had also been exposed recently by
BBC; and
(d) if so, the action taken by
Government to apprehend the human
traffickers?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

83
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Bacterial contamination in rivers
*243. SHRI MAHENDRA
MOHAN:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the  PRIME MINISTER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Pollution
Control Board (CPCB) has recently
revealed that most of the rivers and water
bodies in the country contain an alarming
level of bacterial contamination;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) whether the CPCB has since
proposed any steps to check the filth of
rivers and to prevent them from bacterial
contamination; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Criteria for determining the BPL
†*244. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that several
international financial institutions have
now adopted the limit of income at the
rates of 1.25 and 1.35 dollars per day,
instead of one dollar a day, for determining
the criteria in regard to people living below
poverty line;
(b) if so, the facts thereof and whether
at present the above criteria are being
followed in India; and
(c) the expected decrease in the number
of people living below poverty line in India
on the basis of the above criteria during the
Eleventh Plan?
Growth rate in the country
†*245. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual
growth rate in the country is expected to
remain between 8 per cent and 7 per cent in
the financial year 2008-09;
(b) if not, the estimated rate;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the annual
growth rate in the foodgrain and industrial
manufacturing sector is expected to remain
lower than the average growth rate;
(d) if so, the facts thereof;
(e) whether it is also a fact that the
increase in average growth rate depends on
the increase in service sector, which in turn
depends on international powers; and
(f) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Bio-medical norms
*246. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA
A. HEPTULLA:
SHRI MAHENDRA
MOHAN:
 Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of prosecutions in case
of violation of bio-medical norms by the
Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
in the country;
(b) whether his Ministry maintains the
data of total number of violations and
prosecutions in the States;
(c) if so, the details thereof;

84
(d) whether Government is  aware that
bio-medical waste in most of the clinics
and hospitals is not being disposed of as
per the norms; and
(e) if so, the reasons therefor?
Four-laning in Assam
*247. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) the four-laning status of East-West
corridor in Assam including the construction
of bridge over Brahmaputra and Rail Over
Bridges (ROBs) along with target fixed and
agencies entrusted, phase-wise;
(b) the four-laning status of Baihatta-
Bandardowa sector of NH-52 under State
capital connectivity programme,
indicating target fixed and agencies
entrusted;
(c) whether his Ministry has finalized
the extension of four-laning from Dibrugarh
to Jairampur to link Stillwell road; and
(d) if so, the details thereof including
progress and target of work?
Pollution free Ganga and Yamuna
*248. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has drawn any
scheme to keep all rivers, including Ganga
and Y amuna, clean and free from pollution;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Bidding norms for National Highway
projects
*249. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
 Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
impose toll for more National Highways
(NHs);
(b) if so, whether Government has also
decided to relax bidding norms for road
projects;
(c) whether NH projects have lost
World Bank funding;
(d) if so, by what time Government is
likely to relax bidding norms for road
projects;
(e) whether imposition of toll for more
NHs has been agreed; and
(f) the reasons for World Bank refusing
to provide loan to NH projects?
Funds under JNNURM
*250. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds allocated under
Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal
Mission (JNNURM) during 2008-09 to
each State/UT, especially Uttar Pradesh;
and
(b) the details of utilization of the funds
in each State/UT till date, especially in
Uttar Pradesh, along with the achievement
of physical and financial targets?

85
Committed liabilities
*251. SHRI BISWAJIT DAIMARY:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether committed liabilities have
been transferred along with the Sports
Infrastructure Scheme;
(b)  if so, the details/name of the
implementing agency;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) the tentative period for fulfilling
liabilities;
(e) whether his Ministry partly met
liabilities during the period 01.04.05 to
31.03.07 for Government sector and
colleges and funds have been distributed
equally on first come first served  basis, if
so, the details thereof, and if not, reason
therefor; and
(f) whether during this period for
committed liabilities, Utilization Certificate
submitted by the agency has been
considered for release, if so, the details
including date of receipt/release and, if not,
the reasons therefor?
Utilisation of funds for NHs in Orissa
*252. SHRI RAMA CHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the funds
allocated for National Highways (NHs)
from Panikoili to Rajamunda and Chandhal
Chhak to Dhubari and Angul in Orissa
could not be utilized because of lack of
interest of his Ministry; and
(b) the details of the total amount
sanctioned?
Loss due to non-implementation of
the contract
*253. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: W ill the  PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether according to the Electricity
Act and Indian Electricity Rules, 1956, de-
pillaring operations/penetration depth in
coal mining is allowed only upto 250
meters;
(b) if so, whether Singareni Collieries
Co. Ltd. (SCCL) has allowed a private
company to penetrate upto 390 meters,
violating the Act/Rules, and the guidelines
of the Director General Mining Safety
(DGMS);
(c) whether violation of Act/Rules has
caused delay resulting  in loss of several
crores of rupees  to Government exchequer
for non-implementation of the contract;
(d) if so, the complete details of loss so
far and whether Government would probe
the matter through CVC/CBI; and
(e) if not, reasons therefor?
Remarks of China on Arunachal
Pradesh
*254. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether China has, recently, rejected
India's assertion that Arunachal Pradesh is
its integral part;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government on
such remarks of the Chinese Government;
(c) whether China has also stated that
they never recognized the Mc Mohan Line
and that the status of the border State was
never officially demarcated;

86
(d) if so, whether Government has taken
up the matter with Chinese Government;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Terror attack in Mumbai
†*255. SHRI PRABHA T JHA: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that clinching
evidences of neighbouring  countries,
particularly Pakistan's hand in the recent
gruesome terror attack on Mumbai, have
been found;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the diplomatic steps being taken by
Government so that Pakistan could be
exposed at the International forum?
Group Housing Societies in Delhi
*256. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
 Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Registrar, Co-op Group
Housing Society has received a number of
complaints of misuse of funds by the
Group Housing Societies in Delhi;
(b) if so, whether one of the Group
Housing Societies is Kashmiri Apartments,
Pitampura, where there is mismanagement
of funds and accounts from 2001 and till
now have not been passed by the General
Body;
(c) whether in spite of several
reminders, the Registrar did not take any
action and the management is continuing
defrauding the accounts; and
(d) if so, the action that has been taken
by the Registrar so far against this society
and also other societies which have been
sent to Registrar?
Maritime merchandise trade
*257. SHRI NARESH GUJRAL: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) country's share in world fleet
amongst maritime nations; and
(b) the steps Government has taken to
increase the percentage share of global
merchandise trade through the maritime
route?
Atomic power stations
†*258. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL: W ill the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of atomic power
stations in the country and their total power
generation capacity;
(b) the actual quantum of power
generation thereof; and
(c) the reasons for difference, if any, in
their capacity and actual generation of
power and the steps taken by Government
to ensure their full power generation
capacity?
Cases investigated by CBI
*259. KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of cases that have been
forwarded by the State Government of
Assam to CBI for investigation since 2001,
along with the list of such cases;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

87
(b) the details of cases that have been
investigated and completed so far;
(c) the number of cases pending with
CBI untouched; and
(d) the details thereof?
Minor forest produce
*260. SHRIMATI T. RA TNA BAI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the Minor Forest Produce in each
State, especially in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the details thereof during the last
four years; and
(c) the steps taken to give supporting
price in this regard especially in Andhra
Pradesh areas?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 12th December, 2008 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 21, 1930 (Saka)
